$comment: Exceptions for scripts/check-prod-audit.mjs. Every Critical/High advisory in `pnpm audit --prod`
must appear here or CI fails. Entries expire; an expired entry fails the same gate. An entry whose
advisory no longer appears also fails, so the list cannot only grow and cannot silently pre-approve
a re-introduction. Removing an entry is the fix in that case.
This list is the state on 2026-08-11, not an endorsement of it. #328 owns clearing it.

2026-08-12: the eight nuxt-closure reasons said core-app's vue-sonner optional peer. Measured wrong — moving vue-sonner to devDependencies changed the --prod audit by zero advisories. The real path is apps/nexus's @sentry/nuxt. An exception list is only worth its reasons.
2026-08-12: `module`, `severity` and `versions` are now checked against what the audit actually
reports, not just declared. `versions` is the installed version(s) the advisory hits. This is
here because the prose could be — and four times was — about a different dependency than the
entry allows: GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 carried a verbatim copy of the neighbouring nanoid reason,
which described a range that entry did not have. Nothing could see that by reading. Now the
audit is asked instead.

2026-10-03: GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv (node-forge) and GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (braces) entered the --prod audit with no patched release, failing every PR. Allowlisted for 30 days with traced paths; the owner approved the exception.

2026-10-24: GHSA-jr5w-w6x2-84p9 (electron) and GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (zod 3.25.76) entered the --prod audit with no patch on the installed lines, failing every PR alongside dompurify, body-parser and undici advisories that the same change patched. Allowlisted for 30 days with traced paths; the owner approved the exception. GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (braces) was withdrawn on 2026-10-23 and its entry removed.

2026-11-15: the fifteen entries dated 2026-11-09 (nuxt, simple-git, @simple-git/argv-parser, source-map-js, proxy-addr, @vue/server-renderer, tinypool, sharp) expired and failed every PR into master. Renewed unchanged for 30 days to unblock merges; the owner approved the renewal. The dependency upgrades that remove them follow in a separate PR.

2026-11-15: Cleared source-map-js, proxy-addr, @vue/server-renderer, tinypool and sharp after raising their patched dependency floors. packages/test keeps Vitest in devDependencies because it is a test-only workspace. simple-git and @simple-git/argv-parser stay: their only fix is simple-git 4.x, which drops the default export @nuxt/devtools 3.4.2 imports, and @nuxt/devtools 3.4.3+ (which no longer depends on simple-git) needs @nuxt/kit ^4.5.1, outside the nuxt family pinned at 4.4.8 by #1098. Nuxt remains blocked by the measured unhead 2.1.15 to 3.x migration (#1098).

2026-11-18: GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (picomatch 2.3.2, 4.0.5) entered the --prod audit with patched_versions: null (no upstream fix published yet), failing every PR. Allowlisted for 30 days with traced paths; remove once picomatch ships a patched release.
2026-11-22: GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (picomatch) no longer matches a live advisory in pnpm audit --prod and its allowlist entry was removed.

2026-11-22: Renewed GHSA-jr5w-w6x2-84p9 (electron 41.10.7) for 30 days (to 2026-12-23) with owner approval; no patched 41.x release exists and leaving Electron 41 requires a dedicated major-upgrade validation batch.

2026-11-26: Completed the Nuxt 4.5.2 / unhead 3.x migration (#1098) and bumped @nuxt/devtools 3.4.2 -> 3.4.3 (which drops simple-git). Cleared all 5 nuxt HIGH advisories and all 4 simple-git / @simple-git/argv-parser CRITICAL/HIGH advisories, removing their 9 allowlist entries. Only Electron 41 remains.

advisories.reason: The runtime the packaged app ships. Reaches --prod through the root package.json's electron ^41.10.6 dependency and through @electron-toolkit/preload and @electron-toolkit/utils, production dependencies of @talex-touch/core-app that take electron as a peer (`pnpm audit --prod --json`, 3 paths). The advisory is Chromium's distrust of compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates: until the runtime moves, the app's network stack still accepts certificates chained to them. No 41.x release carries the fix (patched in 42.11.16, 43.8.1, 44.9.1 and 45.0.0-beta.6), and leaving Electron 41 is a major upgrade with its own native-module and packaging verification. Remove this entry when core-app moves to a patched major.
